personalitySettings.title: Assistant tone & response style
personalitySettings.maxOutputTokensNote: Caps how long a single response can be — lower is faster and more battery-friendly on phone hardware.
personalitySettings.deepResearchNote: Breaks your question into sub-questions, researches each separately, then synthesizes one answer. Several sequential model calls on the same model — noticeably slower than a normal reply, not multiple AI models running at once. Independent from the response style above: it changes how much research goes into an answer, not its tone — the two combine (e.g. Deep Research + Succinct still synthesizes a short final answer).
personalitySettings.adaptiveRoutingNote: Classifies each message and picks which downloaded model answers it (e.g. a lightweight model for small talk, a stronger one for research/comparison questions), switching between them as needed. On by default and independent from Deep Research — if it fails for any reason, chat falls back to your normal active model automatically, it never leaves you without a response.

keyStore.dbKeyCorrupt: The stored database encryption key is damaged or has an unexpected format. Fail-closed: NIDO will not overwrite it or open the database without it. If this keeps happening, reinstalling is the only recovery (existing local data cannot be decrypted without the original key).
keyStore.dbKeyReadFailed: NIDO could not read the database encryption key from the secure store. Fail-closed: no new key will be created, because that would permanently lock your existing encrypted data. Restart the app and try again.
keyStore.dbKeyWriteFailed: NIDO generated a new database encryption key but could not save it to the secure store. Fail-closed: the unsaved key was discarded and will not be used. Restart the app and try again — if this keeps happening, the device's secure storage may be damaged.
keyStore.dbKeyLost: NIDO's database encryption key is missing from the secure store, but encrypted databases still exist on this device. Fail-closed: NIDO will NOT generate a new key silently — that would strand your existing data behind an unreadable database. Your data has NOT been deleted. To use NIDO again you must explicitly choose recovery (existing encrypted data cannot be decrypted without the original key).
keyStore.p2pKeyCorrupt: This device's stored identity key is damaged or has an unexpected format. Fail-closed: NIDO will not replace it silently. Reset the identity to create a new one (you will need to re-pair your contacts).
keyStore.p2pKeyReadFailed: NIDO could not read this device's identity key from the secure store. Fail-closed: no new identity will be created, because that would silently break all your pairings. Restart the app and try again.
keyStore.p2pSignKeyCorrupt: This device's stored message-signing key is damaged or has an unexpected format. Fail-closed: NIDO will not replace it silently. Reset the identity to create a new one.
keyStore.p2pSignKeyReadFailed: NIDO could not read this device's message-signing key from the secure store. Fail-closed: no new signing key will be created. Restart the app and try again.

p2pIdentityRecovery.title: Your identity keys were lost
p2pIdentityRecovery.whatHappened: NIDO found your identity record, but the secret keys that prove it is you are gone from this phone's secure storage (keystore). This can happen after a system update, a security reset, or a failed restore.
p2pIdentityRecovery.consequence: Your old identity cannot be used anymore. Your old peers will no longer recognize you — you must re-pair with every contact. Nothing was sent on your behalf.
p2pIdentityRecovery.archived: Your old identity record was kept in the archive, so you can tell your contacts what happened.
p2pIdentityRecovery.confirmBody: Your old peers will no longer recognize you. Re-pairing with every contact will be required. This cannot be undone.
p2pIdentityRecovery.secondBody: Last chance: your old identity will be retired permanently and archived. Continue?
p2pIdentityRecovery.recovered: ✓ New identity created. Re-pair with your contacts to talk again.

keyRecovery.title: Encryption key lost
keyRecovery.whatHappened: NIDO's database encryption key is missing from this device's secure storage, but encrypted databases were found on the device. NIDO stopped here on purpose: creating a new key silently would lock your existing data behind a database it can never open again.
keyRecovery.notDeleted: Your data has NOT been deleted. The encrypted databases are still on this device, exactly as they were.
keyRecovery.cannotRecoverKey: NIDO cannot recover the missing key, and nothing you do here will bring it back. Without the original key, the existing encrypted data cannot be decrypted — by you or by NIDO.
keyRecovery.confirmBody: Recovery keeps the unreadable encrypted databases as archives (in case the original key ever reappears) and lets NIDO start as a new installation with a new key. The archived data cannot be read without the original key. This is the only way to use NIDO again.
keyRecovery.recoveryFailed: Recovery could not be completed safely. Nothing else was touched. You can try again.

aboutScreen.title: About NIDO
aboutScreen.airGappedBody: NIDO is your personal AI assistant that runs entirely on your phone — no account, no cloud, no servers. Your questions, documents, and chats stay on this device.
aboutScreen.hardwareBody: NIDO is designed to run on a phone: it keeps memory use low and watches storage so the app stays fast and responsive.
aboutScreen.benchmarkBody: NIDO measures every answer on your own phone: model load time, time to first token, tokens/sec, peak memory and which sources were used. Run the built-in evaluation from Execution Telemetry → 🧪 Evaluate to compare any installed model on the same questions, or drive it from a computer with npm run eval:device.
aboutScreen.backupBody: Create an encrypted backup, view your encryption key or rotate it.
aboutScreen.limitsBody: NIDO runs AI models inside your phone. They can be wrong or make things up, and smaller models more often. Do not rely on NIDO alone for health, legal, financial or safety decisions: check with a professional or a trusted source.
aboutScreen.privacyBody: NIDO has no accounts, no analytics and no servers of its own. The only connections it makes are the downloads you start (models and knowledge packs), and they are listed in the network log above. The full privacy policy and terms of use are in PRIVACY.md and TERMS.md in the repository.

nido.offlineQueued: out of reach · messages are queued encrypted
nido.noContactsBody: Pair your first contact in the Contacts tab: show your QR code and paste theirs as text.
nido.howItWorksBody: Messages are encrypted on your phone and travel straight to the other NIDO over Bluetooth — no internet, no servers. If your contact isn’t within reach, the message stays in an encrypted queue and is sent only when they appear.
nido.troubleshootBody:
If it won’t connect, try in this order:

1. Open NIDO on this screen on both tablets and tap Connect on either one.
2. Turn on Bluetooth on both. If Bluetooth fails, put both on the same Wi-Fi network (no internet needed): NIDO uses local Wi-Fi as a fallback.
3. Restart both tablets.
4. In Android Settings → Bluetooth, pair the tablets with each other.
5. If it disconnects in background: Settings → Apps → NIDO → Battery → Unrestricted.

nido.batteryHintBody: Android puts NIDO to sleep after a while to save battery, and the link with your contacts drops until you open it again. Let NIDO run in the background (it uses very little battery).
nido.batteryHintManual: Go to Android Settings → Apps → NIDO → Battery → Unrestricted.

settings.sealedHelloDesc: When this phone calls a paired NIDO that supports it, the first messages are sealed so nobody nearby can see who is calling. On by default; with an older NIDO nothing changes.
settings.ratchetV5Desc: Every message gets its own key, like Signal's Double Ratchet: a key stolen today does not open earlier messages. rotateErrors.staging: Couldn't prepare the key change. Nothing was changed.
rotateErrors.storeFailed: Couldn't save the new key; the previous one was kept.

backup.noLockBody: Without a PIN or fingerprint, NIDO can't protect your key: anyone with the phone could see it. We'll show it anyway so you can save it. We recommend setting a PIN in Android settings.

errors.invalid: The file isn't a valid backup.
errors.rollback: Couldn't restore; your previous data was left as it was.
errors.keyFormat: The backup key must be 64 hexadecimal characters.
errors.noDeviceKey: This phone has no encryption key available. Use “Restore with the backup's key”.
errors.wrongKey: The key doesn't open this backup. Check that it's the key you saved when you created it.

backup.warning: Important: store the backup file and your key in different places. If you lose the key, nobody (not even NIDO) can recover your data.
backup.rotateBody: This creates a new key and re-encrypts your database. Earlier backups can NOT be restored with the new key. Continue?
backup.rotatedBody: Your database now uses a new encryption key. Save the new key from “View my encryption key”. Older backups will need the previous key.
backup.rotateFailed: The key could not be rotated.
backup.createFirst: Create a backup first with the button above.
backup.noPermission: Without permission the backup cannot be saved.
backup.savedBody:
Backup copied to the folder you chose:
{{files}}
backup.saveFailed: The backup could not be saved.
backup.keyFailed: The key could not be read.
backup.restoreWithKeyTitle: Restore a backup from another phone
backup.restoreWithKeyBody: Use this when the backup was made on another phone, on an earlier install, or before you rotated your key. Paste the key you saved when you created that backup, then choose the file. This replaces ALL your current data.
backup.keyInvalid: The key must be 64 characters, using only 0–9 and a–f.

remoteTasks.hint: A paired NIDO contact asked your NIDO to do something. Nothing runs until you decide, and approving only records your decision.
remoteTasks.approved: Task from {{sender}} approved. Nothing was executed automatically.

networkLog.title: NETWORK LOG
networkLog.body: Every network request NIDO makes is recorded here. Entries never contain your content: only the host and path, sizes, time and outcome.

skillsCard.title: What the agent can do
skillsCard.body: Step-by-step skills NIDO can follow. Actions that change something always ask you first.

securityStatus.title: Security check
securityStatus.body: Checks on this phone that your data is really protected. It never shows keys.
securityStatus.runFailed: The check could not be run.
securityStatus.vault: Hardware protection (fingerprint or PIN for your data)
securityStatus.vaultHint: Strongest protection: make a backup, then turn on Settings → Security → Hardware protection. Your data will only open with your fingerprint, PIN or pattern.

agentPermissions.historyBody: Every tool the agent used or tried to use. Only the tool name and the result are kept, never the content. It is stored encrypted on this phone and you can delete it.
agentPermissions.toolsBody: Turn off any tool you do not want the agent to use. Actions that change something keep asking you first; that cannot be turned off.
agentPermissions.undoNoteBody: The note the agent saved will be deleted.
agentPermissions.undoReminderBody: The reminder the agent created will be deleted.
agentPermissions.undoFailed: The action could not be undone.
agentPermissions.clearBody: Delete the list of agent actions? Your notes and reminders are not affected.

scheduledTasks.title: Scheduled tasks
scheduledTasks.body: Something the agent does on its own at a set time, like a morning summary of your notes. Tasks run while NIDO is open; if it is closed at that time, your phone shows a notice and the task runs when you open the app. A task can read your notes, calendar and inbox and save notes. It can never send messages, call, pair or open other apps.
scheduledTasks.empty: You have no scheduled tasks yet.
scheduledTasks.loadFailed: Your tasks could not be loaded.
scheduledTasks.instructionPlaceholder: What should the agent do? (for example: Summarize my notes from yesterday)
scheduledTasks.badTime: Write the time as hour:minute, for example 07:30.
scheduledTasks.missingFields: Write a name and what the agent should do.
scheduledTasks.createFailed: The task could not be saved.
scheduledTasks.limit: You can have up to {{max}} tasks.
scheduledTasks.notifyFailedBody: The task could not be completed. Open NIDO to see it.
scheduledTasks.notifyDueBody: A scheduled task is ready. Open NIDO to run it.

crashReport.title: Crash diagnostics
crashReport.body: If NIDO closed by itself, the reason Android recorded shows up here. Copy the report and paste it into a bug report: it does not include your messages, notes or memory.

vault.offerTitle: Protect your data with your fingerprint or PIN
vault.offerBody: Turn on hardware protection: the key to your data stays in the tablet's security chip and only opens with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint. It is NIDO's strongest protection.
vault.offerConfirmHint: Before you confirm: if you ever remove the screen lock, NIDO cannot open your data without a backup and its key. We recommend making a backup first (About → Open backup).
vault.title: Hardware protection
vault.body: Protects NIDO's data with the tablet's security chip: it only opens with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint. If someone takes the tablet powered off or rebooted, they can't read your NIDO data even if they extract it.
vault.promptSubtitle: Confirm with your PIN or fingerprint
vault.confirmBody:
Your NIDO data will only open with this tablet's PIN, pattern or fingerprint.

Important: if you ever REMOVE the tablet's screen lock, Android deletes this key and NIDO won't be able to open your data; you can only recover it from a backup and its key.

Recommended: create a backup first (About → Open backup).
vault.deactivateBody: Your data's key will be stored again without requiring your PIN or fingerprint.
vault.errNoLock: Set a PIN, pattern or password on the tablet to turn on hardware protection.
vault.errUnavailable: Hardware protection isn't available in this build of NIDO.
vault.errStatus: Couldn't check hardware protection on this device: {{reason}}
vault.errVerify: Verification failed and nothing was changed. Your data is unchanged.
vault.errGeneric: Couldn't complete it. Nothing was changed.
vault.lockSubtitle: Your data is protected by the security chip. Unlock with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint.
vault.keyInvalidated: Android invalidated NIDO's security key (usually because the screen lock was removed). Your data can't be opened without a backup.
vault.promptVerify: Confirm once more to verify the protection
vault.errUnsupported: Hardware protection requires Android 11 or later.
vault.rewrapProtect: Confirm to protect the new key
vault.rewrapVerify: Confirm once more to verify it
vault.strictBody: If you leave NIDO (or turn the screen off) for longer than the chosen time, NIDO closes completely and wipes the key and your data from memory. So even if the tablet is stolen while on, there's nothing left to extract. While closed you won't receive P2P messages: your contacts keep them and they arrive when you open NIDO again.
vault.strictConfirm: NIDO will close completely when you leave the app for longer than the chosen time, and you'll need to unlock it again. While closed you won't receive P2P messages (they arrive when you open it).

multilingual.title: Spanish & Portuguese search
multilingual.body: Understands questions in Spanish and Portuguese and finds the right articles even when they're written in English. Downloads a 126 MB model and rebuilds the search index in the background; keyword search keeps working meanwhile. Everything stays on this device.
multilingual.statusOn: On: multilingual search model in use.
multilingual.enabled: Done. Search now understands Spanish and Portuguese.
multilingual.disabled: Back to the English-only search model.
multilingual.confirmOnBody: NIDO will download a 126 MB model (only once) and rebuild the search index in the background. It can take a few minutes and you can keep chatting. If you use the Wikipedia Vital pack, download its multilingual version below to search it in Spanish or Portuguese.
multilingual.confirmOffBody: NIDO will go back to the English-only search model and rebuild the search index in the background.
multilingual.packOtherModel: Made for the other search model: only keyword search works with this pack right now.

guide.title: Learn to use NIDO
guide.subtitle: Tap an example and it's typed into the chat, ready to send. Nothing is sent on its own.
guide.toolOff: This feature is turned off in $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.about) → $t(agentPermissions.toolsTitle). Turn it on there to try it.
guide.helpBody: A short guide with examples you can tap to try each feature.

onboarding.s1Body: Your private agent. I live on your device, not in the cloud: no accounts, no tracking, and once installed I work without internet.
onboarding.s2Body: Tap an example: it's typed into the chat and you decide when to send it.
onboarding.s2Wait: The first answer can take a few seconds while I get ready.
s2Examples: remind me to drink water in 1 hour
onboarding.s3Body: I search Wikipedia without internet, read your documents, remind you of things, talk to another NIDO over Bluetooth and protect your data with your tablet's security chip.

lessons.title: Talk to NIDO
lessons.what: Chat like you would with anyone. Greetings and small talk get an instant answer.
lessons.tip: For everything else NIDO uses its AI model, which lives on your device: it can take a few seconds.

lessons.title: Time, math and conversions
lessons.what: Exact answers: the time comes from your device and the math is done by the app, not the AI model.
lessons.tip: The calculator understands +, -, *, /, %, powers (^), sqrt and pi, up to 50 characters.

lessons.title: Reminders
lessons.what: NIDO notifies you at the time you say, even if the app is closed.
examples: remind me to call mom tomorrow at 5
remind me to buy milk in 2 hours
lessons.tip: Say when: “tomorrow”, “on Friday”, “in 30 minutes”. If you don't, NIDO asks.

lessons.title: Notes
lessons.what: Save quick notes, encrypted on your device.
examples: take a note: ideas for Ana's birthday
note: water the plants on Sunday
lessons.tip: One word from the title is enough to open a note.

lessons.title: Memory
lessons.what: Your memory works like this. What you tell me is kept in four drawers: Facts holds things about you, like your name, where you live or your favorite color. People holds everyone else: your mom, your partner, your friends. Notes holds what you ask me to write down, word for word. And Reminders holds anything with a date or a time. You can also ask me back in your own words: “What's my mom's name?”, “What's my favorite color?”. I answer from what you told me. Everything lives on this device, encrypted. Nothing is uploaded to any server, and whatever you want deleted, gets deleted.
lessons.tip: “Remember that…” saves a fact. “Remind me…” sets an alert. See and delete what's saved in the menu → $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.memory).

lessons.title: Calendar
lessons.what: Check your events and add new ones to your device's calendar.
lessons.tip: Before creating an event NIDO shows it to you and asks you to confirm. Needs calendar permission.

lessons.title: Contacts and calls
lessons.what: Search your contacts and call without looking up the number.
lessons.tip: Before calling NIDO shows you the number and asks you to confirm. Needs contacts permission.

lessons.title: Ask without internet
lessons.what: NIDO answers with Wikipedia articles stored on your device and shows you the sources.
examples: how do plants make their food?
lessons.tip: Just ask normally; if nothing comes up, try the keyword. For 50,000 articles download “Wikipedia Vital” in $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.knowledgeBase).

lessons.title: Your documents
lessons.what: Import your documents and ask about them.
steps: Go to $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.knowledgeBase) → $t(corpusSettingsTab.yourDocuments).
Import a PDF, .txt or .md file.
Ask about its content.
examples: what does my document say about the renewal?
lessons.tip: PDFs need selectable text: scanned images can't be read.

lessons.title: Spanish and Portuguese search
lessons.what: Understands questions in Spanish and Portuguese and finds the right article even when it's in English.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.knowledgeBase) → “$t(multilingual.title)” → $t(multilingual.turnOn) (downloads a 126 MB model, once).
Wait for “Preparing search”: you can keep chatting meanwhile.
Optional: download “Wikipedia Vital (multilingual search)”, about 156 MB.
lessons.tip: New installs in Spanish or Portuguese have it on from the start.

lessons.title: Links and files
lessons.what: Open links and analyze files on your device, like a CSV table.
lessons.tip: NIDO asks you to confirm before opening a link, and you pick the file.

lessons.title: NIDO to NIDO
lessons.what: Encrypted messages straight to another NIDO over Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi, without internet or servers.
steps: Open the menu → NIDO on both tablets.
In the $t(nido.tabContacts) tab, show your QR code and paste the other one as text.
Check the verification fingerprint together.
In the $t(nido.tabLink) tab tap $t(nido.connectButton) on either tablet and write in $t(nido.tabChats).
lessons.tip: If the other NIDO is out of range, the message waits encrypted and is sent when it shows up. If it disconnects after a while with NIDO closed, tap “Allow” on the battery notice in the NIDO screen.

lessons.title: NIDO from any app
lessons.what: Use NIDO without opening it first.
steps: Share → NIDO: select text in any app, tap Share and pick NIDO. A new chat opens with the text typed in, not sent.
Long-press the NIDO icon for New chat and NIDO messages.
Add the “Ask NIDO” tile to your Quick Settings (edit Quick Settings).

lessons.title: Voice
lessons.what: Dictate your messages and, if you like, hear the answers.
steps: Tap the microphone in the chat bar and speak.
To hear answers: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.voice) → $t(voiceSettings.readAloudLabel).
lessons.tip: Needs microphone permission. Dictation depends on your device's speech recognition.

lessons.title: Everything on your device
lessons.what: Your chats, notes, memory and documents are stored encrypted on your device. After install, NIDO works without internet; it only connects when you download a model or a pack.
examples: Where do you store my data?
lessons.tip: In $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.about) you can see NIDO's network log.

lessons.title: Hardware protection
lessons.what: Lock your data with your tablet's security chip: it only opens with your PIN or fingerprint.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.security) → $t(vault.title) → $t(vault.activate).
lessons.tip: Your tablet needs a PIN, pattern or password. Make a backup before turning it on.

lessons.title: Backup
lessons.what: Keep an encrypted copy of your data so you don't lose it if you change tablets.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.recovery) → Backup → $t(backup.createButton).
Copy and keep the key it shows you: without it the backup can't be opened.
Share the file to a safe place.

lessons.title: Erase everything
lessons.what: Delete all your data from the device and start over.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.recovery) → $t(modelSetupScreen.recovery.dangerBadge).
lessons.tip: This can't be undone. If you want to keep something, make a backup first.

lessons.title: Choose a model
lessons.what: Change the AI model for your device: small ones are fast, big ones reason better and use more memory.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.models).
lessons.tip: If answers take too long or the app closes, try a smaller model.

lessons.title: Tone
lessons.what: Choose how NIDO talks to you: shorter, more detailed, or with your own instructions.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.settings) → $t(modelSetupScreen.sections.tone).

lessons.title: If something fails
lessons.what: If NIDO closes on its own, next time you can see why and copy it to report it.
steps: $t(chatScreen.drawerItems.about) → $t(crashReport.title).
Report the problem on GitHub, in the NIDO repository's Issues.

exactAlarm.title: Reminders on time
exactAlarm.ok: Reminders arrive at the exact time.
exactAlarm.off: Android may delay your reminders by a few minutes while the phone is idle. To get them at the exact time, allow “Alarms & reminders” for NIDO.

licenses.title: Licenses
licenses.intro: NIDO is open-source software. This is what each license that applies to the app, and to what you download with it, says. Links are for copying: NIDO does not open the internet.
licenses.appBody: MIT License. NIDO is based on BOAR (also MIT); both copyright notices are in the text below.
licenses.modelsBody: They are not inside the app: they are downloaded from their publishers when you choose them, and each keeps its own license.
licenses.knowledgeBody: The app carries 300 Wikipedia article introductions, and the optional knowledge packs carry more. Text by Wikipedia contributors (wikipedia.org), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Every answer that uses it shows its article URL. The Wikipedia packs compiled by NIDO are shared under the same license; the NIDO Essentials guides, written by NIDO, are CC BY 4.0. NIDO is not affiliated with the Wikimedia Foundation.
licenses.embeddingNote: The multilingual search model (multilingual-e5-small, by intfloat) is MIT, Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation; NIDO publishes its GGUF conversion with that notice.
licenses.thirdPartyBody: {{count}} open-source packages. Tap one to read its license.
licenses.thirdPartyPartial: This build does not include the third-party license texts; they are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the repository.
licenses.noText: This package ships no license file; the license it declares applies.

notes.lfm: Not Apache or MIT: commercial use is only allowed for entities with under USD 10 million in annual revenue, and anyone who redistributes it must give a copy of the license.
notes.ccBySa: You may share and adapt it by crediting Wikipedia (and NIDO as compiler of the packs), linking the license, indicating changes and keeping CC BY-SA 4.0.
notes.ccByNido: Guides written by NIDO from public guidance by the Red Cross, the AHA, the WHO and other organizations, which have not reviewed them and do not endorse NIDO. You may share and adapt them, crediting NIDO. General information only: not a substitute for a first aid course; in an emergency, call your emergency number.

panic.buttonLabel: Panic button: hold 3 seconds to erase everything
panic.buttonHint: Erases all NIDO data: chats, contacts, keys, memory and models. It cannot be undone. With TalkBack, the long-press action erases at once.
panic.settingDesc: Shows a wipe button (a red shield) on the main screen. Holding it for 3 seconds erases all NIDO data at once, without asking for fingerprint or confirmation. It cannot be undone; make a backup first if you want to keep anything.

emergency.title: Emergency
emergency.noPackBody: To see your country's checked emergency numbers here, download the NIDO Local pack (about 0.2 MB).
emergency.noCountryBody: Pick another country or ask in the chat.
emergency.describeHint: NIDO answers from the guides on your phone, without internet.
emergency.disclaimer: If someone is in danger, call first. NIDO does not replace emergency services.
